    <protocol>VisionRequest</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>A request that produces a mask of individual people it finds in the input image.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

The request returns the resulting image mask in an instance of [InstanceMaskObservation](ref:vision/instancemaskobservation).

## Topics

### Creating a request

[init(_:)](ref:vision/generatepersoninstancemaskrequest/init(_:))
`init(GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest.Revision?)`
Creates a person instance mask request.

### Performing a request

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-80bya)
`func perform(on: URL, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on an image URL and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-3f3f1)
`func perform(on: Data, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on image data and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-qxxx)
`func perform(on: CGImage, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a Core Graphics image and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-xspx)
`func perform(on: CVPixelBuffer, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a pixel buffer and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-3hddl)
`func perform(on: CMSampleBuffer, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a Core Media buffer and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-85ex1)
`func perform(on: CIImage, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a Core Image image and produces observations.

### Understanding the result

[InstanceMaskObservation](ref:vision/instancemaskobservation)
`struct InstanceMaskObservation`
An observation that contains an instance mask that labels instances in the mask.

### Getting the revision

[revision](ref:vision/generatepersoninstancemaskrequest/revision-swift.property)
`let revision: GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest.Revision`
The algorithm or implementation the request uses.

[supportedRevisions](ref:vision/generatepersoninstancemaskrequest/supportedrevisions)
`static let supportedRevisions: [GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest.Revision]`
The collection of revisions the request supports.

[GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest.Revision](ref:vision/generatepersoninstancemaskrequest/revision-swift.enum)
`enum Revision`
A type that describes the algorithm or implementation that the request performs.

## See Also

### Image segmentation and subject lifting

[Segmenting objects using taps, scribbles or rectangles](ref:vision/segmenting-objects-using-taps-scribbles-or-rectangles)
Select objects or regions in a photo using taps, scribbles, or rectangle selection, and generate a segmentation mask using the iterative segmentation API.

[GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest](ref:vision/generateforegroundinstancemaskrequest)
`struct GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest`
A request that generates an instance mask of noticeable objects to separate from the background.

[GeneratePersonSegmentationRequest](ref:vision/generatepersonsegmentationrequest)
`class GeneratePersonSegmentationRequest`
A request that produces a matte image for a person it finds in the input image.

[GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest](ref:vision/generateiterativesegmentationrequest)
`class GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`
A request that generates a segmentation mask from points, a rectangle, or a scribble.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/ocrtool">
<title>OCRTool (Vision)</title>
<kind>Structure</kind>
<availability>iOS 27.0+, iPadOS 27.0+, Mac Catalyst 27.0+, macOS 27.0+, visionOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">struct OCRTool</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
  <conformsTo title="Conforms To">
    <protocol>Tool</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>A tool that recognizes text in an image.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

The tool returns a string containing all recognized text from the image. To enable this tool, configure your `LanguageModelSession` with an instance of `OCRTool`.

```swift
let ocrTool = OCRTool()
let session = LanguageModelSession(tools: [ocrTool])
```

You can override the default name and description to customize how the model identifies and uses the tool.

```swift
let customTool = OCRTool(
    name: "extractText",
    description: "Extract text from documents"
)
```

> **Note:** [OCRTool](ref:vision/ocrtool) isn’t available in Simulator.

## Topics

### Creating a tool

[init(name:description:)](ref:vision/ocrtool/init(name:description:))
`init(name: String?, description: String?)`
Creates a tool for recognizing text in images.

## See Also

### Foundation Models integration

[BarcodeReaderTool](ref:vision/barcodereadertool)
`struct BarcodeReaderTool`
A tool that scans machine-readable codes in an image.
</content>
</document>

<purpose>An image-analysis request to scan an image of a document and provide information about its structure.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

This request scans a document and extracts different groups of text and barcodes within the document image. Use this request to understand different types of structured texts like receipts, nutritional labels, textbook pages, forms, or other documents that you want to understand in further detail.

The request generates a [DocumentObservation](ref:vision/documentobservation) array, which allows you to access your chosen document’s structure grouped by words, lines, or paragraphs. You can also access tables and lists that appear in the document.

<document id="vision/recognizetextrequest">
<title>RecognizeTextRequest (Vision)</title>
<kind>Structure</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">struct RecognizeTextRequest</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
  <conformsTo title="Conforms To">
    <protocol>CustomStringConvertible</protocol>
    <protocol>ImageProcessingRequest</protocol>
    <protocol>VisionRequest</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>An image-analysis request that recognizes text in an image.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

This request generates a collection of [RecognizedTextObservation](ref:vision/recognizedtextobservation) objects that describe the text the request detects. By default, a text-recognition request first locates all possible glyphs or characters in the input image, and then analyzes each string. To specify or limit the languages to find in the request, set [recognitionLanguages](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/recognitionlanguages) to an array that contains the names of the languages of text you want to recognize.

## Topics

### Creating a request

[init(_:)](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/init(_:))
`init(RecognizeTextRequest.Revision?)`
Creates a text-recognition request.

### Performing a request

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-80bya)
`func perform(on: URL, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on an image URL and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-3f3f1)
`func perform(on: Data, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on image data and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-qxxx)
`func perform(on: CGImage, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a Core Graphics image and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-xspx)
`func perform(on: CVPixelBuffer, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a pixel buffer and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-3hddl)
`func perform(on: CMSampleBuffer, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a Core Media buffer and produces observations.

[perform(on:orientation:)](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest/perform(on:orientation:)-85ex1)
`func perform(on: CIImage, orientation: CGImagePropertyOrientation?) async throws -> Self.Result`
Performs the request on a Core Image image and produces observations.

### Understanding the result

[RecognizedTextObservation](ref:vision/recognizedtextobservation)
`struct RecognizedTextObservation`
An object that contains information about both the location and content of text and glyphs that the framework recognizes in an image.

### Configuring a request

[automaticallyDetectsLanguage](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/automaticallydetectslanguage)
`var automaticallyDetectsLanguage: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether to attempt detecting the language to use the appropriate model for recognition and language correction.

[usesLanguageCorrection](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/useslanguagecorrection)
`var usesLanguageCorrection: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether the request applies language correction during the recognition process.

[supportedRecognitionLanguages](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/supportedrecognitionlanguages)
`var supportedRecognitionLanguages: [Locale.Language]`
The identifiers of the languages that the request supports.

[customWords](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/customwords)
`var customWords: [String]`
An array of strings to supplement the recognized languages at the word-recognition stage.

[minimumTextHeightFraction](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/minimumtextheightfraction)
`var minimumTextHeightFraction: Float`
The minimum height, relative to the image height, of the text to recognize.

[recognitionLanguages](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/recognitionlanguages)
`var recognitionLanguages: [Locale.Language]`
An array of languages to detect, in priority order.

[recognitionLevel](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/recognitionlevel-swift.property)
`var recognitionLevel: RecognizeTextRequest.RecognitionLevel`
A value that determines whether the request prioritizes accuracy or speed in text recognition.

[RecognizeTextRequest.RecognitionLevel](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/recognitionlevel-swift.enum)
`enum RecognitionLevel`
Constants that identify the performance and accuracy of the text recognition.

### Getting the revision

[revision](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/revision-swift.property)
`let revision: RecognizeTextRequest.Revision`
The algorithm or implementation the request uses.

[supportedRevisions](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/supportedrevisions)
`static let supportedRevisions: [RecognizeTextRequest.Revision]`
The collection of revisions the request supports.

[RecognizeTextRequest.Revision](ref:vision/recognizetextrequest/revision-swift.enum)
`enum Revision`
A type that describes the algorithm or implementation that the request performs.

## See Also

### Text and document analysis

Perform text recognition on a photo using the Vision framework’s text-recognition request.

Scan a document that contains a table and extract its content in a formatted way.

A request that detects barcodes in an image.

`struct DetectDocumentSegmentationRequest`
A request that detects rectangular regions that contain text in the input image.

`struct DetectTextRectanglesRequest`
An image-analysis request that finds regions of visible text in an image.

[RecognizeDocumentsRequest](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest)
`struct RecognizeDocumentsRequest`
An image-analysis request to scan an image of a document and provide information about its structure.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/computestage">

<kind>Enumeration</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">enum ComputeStage</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Types that represent the compute stage.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

The main compute stage represents the essential functionality of a request. Requests that provide additional analysis — or conversion of the data by the main stage — can also report a post-processing stage.

## Topics

### Getting the compute stages

[ComputeStage.main](ref:vision/computestage)
`case main`
A stage that represents where the system performs the main functionality.

[ComputeStage.postProcessing](ref:vision/computestage)
`case postProcessing`
A stage that represents where the system performs additional analysis after the main compute stage.

[CoreMLModelContainer](ref:vision/coremlmodelcontainer)
`struct CoreMLModelContainer`
A model container to use with an image-analysis request.

[cropAndScaleAction](ref:vision/coremlrequest/cropandscaleaction)

An optional setting that tells the Vision algorithm how to scale an input image.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)

A scale to apply to an input image before performing a request.

`case revision3`
An algorithm or implementation that represents the third revision.

[DetectFaceLandmarksRequest.Revision.revision4](ref:vision/detectfacelandmarksrequest/revision-swift.enum/revision4)
`case revision4`
This revision uses [DetectFaceRectanglesRequest.Revision.revision4](ref:vision/detectfacerectanglesrequest/revision-swift.enum/revision4) for detecting faces and then detects 98 face landmark points, providing more detailed results than the previous revision. This is the default revision on platforms that support it. Specify `.revision3` at instantiation to preserve the previous behavior. Use [supportedRevisions](ref:vision/detectfacelandmarksrequest/supportedrevisions) to check if this revision is supported on the platform.

<document id="vision/downloadableassetsrequeststatus">
<title>DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus (Vision)</title>
<kind>Enumeration</kind>
<availability>iOS 27.0+, iPadOS 27.0+, Mac Catalyst 27.0+, macOS 27.0+, tvOS 27.0+, visionOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">enum DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The status of the assets required by a [DownloadableAssetsRequest](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest).</purpose>
<content>
## Topics

### Download status cases

[DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus.error(_:)](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequeststatus)
`case error(any Error)`
The asset download failed with an error.

[DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus.notReady](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequeststatus)
`case notReady`
The assets are not ready or the status is unknown. Call [downloadAssets()](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest/downloadassets()) or [downloadAssets(progress:)](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest/downloadassets(progress:)) to initiate the download.

[DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus.ready](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequeststatus)
`case ready`
The assets are ready.

[DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus.downloading](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequeststatus)
`case downloading`
The assets are being downloaded. Check progress through the subprogress that was passed to [downloadAssets(progress:)](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest/downloadassets(progress:)).

## See Also

### Protocols

[ImageProcessingRequest](ref:vision/imageprocessingrequest)
`protocol ImageProcessingRequest`
A type for image-analysis requests that focus on a specific part of an image.

[PoseProviding](ref:vision/poseproviding)
`protocol PoseProviding`
An observation that provides a collection of joints that make up a pose.

[StatefulRequest](ref:vision/statefulrequest)
`protocol StatefulRequest`
The protocol for a type that builds evidence of a condition over time.

[TargetedRequest](ref:vision/targetedrequest)
`protocol TargetedRequest`
A type for analyzing two images together.

[VisionObservation](ref:vision/visionobservation)
`protocol VisionObservation`
A type for objects produced by image-analysis requests.

[VisionRequest](ref:vision/visionrequest)
`protocol VisionRequest`
A type for image-analysis requests.

[DownloadableAssetsRequest](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest)
`protocol DownloadableAssetsRequest`
A request whose execution depends on assets that may need to be downloaded.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/generateiterativesegmentationrequest/qualitylevel-swift.enum">
<title>GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest.QualityLevel (Vision)</title>
<kind>Enumeration</kind>
<availability>iOS 27.0+, iPadOS 27.0+, Mac Catalyst 27.0+, macOS 27.0+, tvOS 27.0+, visionOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">enum QualityLevel</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest</parent>
  <conformsTo title="Conforms To">
    <protocol>CaseIterable</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>The resolution and quality of the segmentation mask the request produces.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

Higher quality levels produce a smoother, higher-resolution mask. Lower quality levels favor speed over resolution.

## Topics

### Quality cases

[GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest.QualityLevel.accurate](ref:vision/generateiterativesegmentationrequest/qualitylevel-swift.enum)
`case accurate`
Produces a high-resolution mask.

[GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest.QualityLevel.balanced](ref:vision/generateiterativesegmentationrequest/qualitylevel-swift.enum)
`case balanced`
Produces a medium-resolution mask that balances speed and accuracy. This is the default setting.

[GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest.QualityLevel.fast](ref:vision/generateiterativesegmentationrequest/qualitylevel-swift.enum)
`case fast`
Produces a low-resolution mask, but runs very quickly.

## See Also

### Accessing the quality level

[qualityLevel](ref:vision/generateiterativesegmentationrequest/qualitylevel-swift.property)
`var qualityLevel: GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest.QualityLevel`
Controls the resolution of the produced mask.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/imagecropandscaleaction">
<title>ImageCropAndScaleAction (Vision)</title>
<kind>Enumeration</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">enum ImageCropAndScaleAction</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
  <conformsTo title="Conforms To">
    <protocol>CaseIterable</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>A scale to apply to an input image before performing a request.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

Scaling an image ensures that it fits within the algorithm’s input image dimensions, which may require a change in aspect ratio. The figure below shows how each crop-and-scale option transforms the input image:

![A series of six photos that show the effects of applying a center crop, scale fit, scale fill, scale fit rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise, and scale fill rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise option to the original input image.](https://developer.apple.com/images/Vision/scale-crop-options@2x.png)

## Topics

### Getting the actions

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.centerCrop](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)
`case centerCrop`
An action that scales the image and maintains the aspect ratio to fit on the short side and crop centered on the long side.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFit](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)
`case scaleToFit`
An action that scales to the size the algorithm requires while maintaining the original aspect ratio.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFill](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)
`case scaleToFill`
An action that scales the image to fill the input dimensions and resizing it, if necessary.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFitPlus90CCWRotation](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction/scaletofitplus90ccwrotation)
`case scaleToFitPlus90CCWRotation`
An action that scales the image and maintains the aspect ratio to fit on the long side, and rotates the image by 90 degrees counter clockwise.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFillPlus90CCWRotation](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction/scaletofillplus90ccwrotation)
`case scaleToFillPlus90CCWRotation`
An action that scales the image and rotates it by 90 degrees counter clockwise.

## See Also

### Configuring a request

[cropAndScaleAction](ref:vision/calculateimageaestheticsscoresrequest/cropandscaleaction)
`var cropAndScaleAction: ImageCropAndScaleAction`
An optional setting that tells the algorithm how to scale an input image before generating the result.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/recognizeanimalsrequest/revision-swift.enum">
<title>RecognizeAnimalsRequest.Revision (Vision)</title>
<kind>Enumeration</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>

<related>
  <parent>RecognizeAnimalsRequest</parent>
  <conformsTo title="Conforms To">
    <protocol>Comparable</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>A type that describes the algorithm or implementation that the request performs.</purpose>
<content>
## Topics

### Getting the revision

[RecognizeAnimalsRequest.Revision.revision2](ref:vision/recognizeanimalsrequest/revision-swift.enum)
`case revision2`
An algorithm or implementation that represents the second revision.

### Enumeration Cases

[RecognizeAnimalsRequest.Revision.revision3](ref:vision/recognizeanimalsrequest/revision-swift.enum/revision3)
`case revision3`
Compared to `.revision2`, this revision generally provides better precision and recall, and can also detect dog and cat heads. This is the default revision on platforms that support it. Specify `.revision2` at instantiation to preserve the previous behavior. Use [supportedRevisions](ref:vision/recognizeanimalsrequest/supportedrevisions) to check if this revision is supported on the platform.

<document id="vision/visionresult">
<title>VisionResult (Vision)</title>
<kind>Enumeration</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">enum VisionResult</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
  <conformsTo title="Conforms To">
    <protocol>Copyable</protocol>
    <protocol>CustomStringConvertible</protocol>
    <protocol>Escapable</protocol>
  </conformsTo>
</related>
<purpose>The result the framework produces by performing a request.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

Each result contains the original [VisionRequest](ref:vision/visionrequest), along with any observations produced.

## Topics

### Getting the still-image result

[VisionResult.classifyImage(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case classifyImage(ClassifyImageRequest, [ClassificationObservation])`
A result from performing a classify image request.

### Getting the image sequence result

[VisionResult.generatePersonInstanceMask(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case generatePersonInstanceMask(GeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest, InstanceMaskObservation?)`
A result from performing a generate person instance mask request.

[VisionResult.generatePersonSegmentation(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case generatePersonSegmentation(GeneratePersonSegmentationRequest, PixelBufferObservation)`
A result from performing a generate person segmentation request.

[VisionResult.detectDocumentSegmentation(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectDocumentSegmentation(DetectDocumentSegmentationRequest, DetectedDocumentObservation?)`
A result from performing a detect document segmentation request.

[VisionResult.generateIterativeSegmentation(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/generateiterativesegmentation(_:_:))
`case generateIterativeSegmentation(GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest, PixelBufferObservation?)`

[VisionResult.recognizeDocuments(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/recognizedocuments(_:_:))
`case recognizeDocuments(RecognizeDocumentsRequest, [DocumentObservation])`

### Getting the iterative and selected object result

[VisionResult.generateIterativeSegmentation(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/generateiterativesegmentation(_:_:))
`case generateIterativeSegmentation(GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest, PixelBufferObservation?)`

### Getting the image aesthetics and lens smudge result

[VisionResult.calculateImageAestheticsScores(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case calculateImageAestheticsScores(CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest, ImageAestheticsScoresObservation)`
A result from performing a calculate image aesthetics scores request.

[VisionResult.detectLensSmudge(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/detectlenssmudge(_:_:))
`case detectLensSmudge(DetectLensSmudgeRequest, SmudgeObservation)`

### Getting the saliency result

[VisionResult.generateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImage(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case generateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImage(GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest, SaliencyImageObservation)`
A result from performing a generate objectness based saliency image request.

[VisionResult.generateAttentionBasedSaliencyImage(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case generateAttentionBasedSaliencyImage(GenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest, SaliencyImageObservation)`
A result from performing a generate attention based saliency image request.

### Getting the object-tracking result

[VisionResult.trackRectangle(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case trackRectangle(TrackRectangleRequest, RectangleObservation?)`
A result from performing a track rectangle request.

[VisionResult.trackObject(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case trackObject(TrackObjectRequest, DetectedObjectObservation?)`
A result from performing a track object request.

### Getting the face and body detection result

[VisionResult.detectFaceCaptureQuality(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectFaceCaptureQuality(DetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest, [FaceObservation])`
A result from performing a detect face capture quality request.

[VisionResult.detectFaceLandmarks(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectFaceLandmarks(DetectFaceLandmarksRequest, [FaceObservation])`
A result from performing a detect face landmarks request.

[VisionResult.detectFaceRectangles(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectFaceRectangles(DetectFaceRectanglesRequest, [FaceObservation])`
A result from performing a detect face rectangles request.

[VisionResult.detectHumanRectangles(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectHumanRectangles(DetectHumanRectanglesRequest, [HumanObservation])`
A result from performing a detect human rectangles request.

### Getting the body and hand pose detection result

[VisionResult.detectHumanBodyPose(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/detecthumanbodypose(_:_:))
`case detectHumanBodyPose(DetectHumanBodyPoseRequest, [HumanBodyPoseObservation])`
A result from performing a detect human body pose request.

[VisionResult.detectHumanHandPose(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/detecthumanhandpose(_:_:))
`case detectHumanHandPose(DetectHumanHandPoseRequest, [HumanHandPoseObservation])`
A result from performing a detect human hand pose request.

[VisionResult.detectHumanBodyPose3D(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/detecthumanbodypose3d(_:_:))
`case detectHumanBodyPose3D(DetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest, [HumanBodyPose3DObservation])`
A result from performing a 3D detect human body pose request.

### Getting the animal detection result

[VisionResult.recognizeAnimals(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case recognizeAnimals(RecognizeAnimalsRequest, [RecognizedObjectObservation])`
A result from performing a recognize animals request.

[VisionResult.detectAnimalBodyPose(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/detectanimalbodypose(_:_:))
`case detectAnimalBodyPose(DetectAnimalBodyPoseRequest, [AnimalBodyPoseObservation])`
A result from performing a detect animal body pose request.

### Getting the text result

[VisionResult.detectTextRectangles(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/detecttextrectangles(_:_:))
`case detectTextRectangles(DetectTextRectanglesRequest, [TextObservation])`
A result from performing a detect text rectangles request.

[VisionResult.recognizeText(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/recognizetext(_:_:))
`case recognizeText(RecognizeTextRequest, [RecognizedTextObservation])`
A result from performing a recognize text request.

### Getting the image alignment, feature print, and background removal result

[VisionResult.trackTranslationalImageRegistration(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case trackTranslationalImageRegistration(TrackTranslationalImageRegistrationRequest, ImageTranslationAlignmentObservation)`
A result from performing a track translational image request.

[VisionResult.trackHomographicImageRegistration(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case trackHomographicImageRegistration(TrackHomographicImageRegistrationRequest, ImageHomographicAlignmentObservation)`
A result from performing a track homographic image request.

[VisionResult.generateForegroundInstanceMask(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case generateForegroundInstanceMask(GenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest, InstanceMaskObservation?)`
A result from performing a generate foreground instance mask request.

[VisionResult.generateImageFeaturePrint(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case generateImageFeaturePrint(GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest, FeaturePrintObservation)`
A result from performing a generate image feature print request.

### Getting the trajectory, contour, and horizon detection result

[VisionResult.detectTrajectories(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectTrajectories(DetectTrajectoriesRequest, [TrajectoryObservation])`
A result from performing a detect trajectories request.

[VisionResult.detectContours(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectContours(DetectContoursRequest, ContoursObservation)`
A result from performing a detect contours request.

[VisionResult.detectHorizon(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectHorizon(DetectHorizonRequest, HorizonObservation?)`
A result from performing a detect horizon request.

### Getting the optical flow, rectangle and barcode detection result

[VisionResult.trackOpticalFlow(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult/trackopticalflow(_:_:))
`case trackOpticalFlow(TrackOpticalFlowRequest, OpticalFlowObservation?)`
A result from performing a track optical flow request.

[VisionResult.detectRectangles(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectRectangles(DetectRectanglesRequest, [RectangleObservation])`
A result from performing a detect rectangles request.

[VisionResult.detectBarcodes(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case detectBarcodes(DetectBarcodesRequest, [BarcodeObservation])`
A result from performing a detect barcodes request.

### Getting the machine learning image-analysis result

[VisionResult.coreML(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case coreML(CoreMLRequest, [any VisionObservation])`
A result from performing a Core ML request.

### Getting the error result

[VisionResult.error(_:_:)](ref:vision/visionresult)
`case error(any VisionRequest, any Error)`
A result from encountering a framework error.

## See Also

### Performing the request

[Result](ref:vision/visionrequest/result)
`associatedtype Result`
An associated type that represents the result.
</content>

Inspect [assetStatus](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest/assetstatus) to determine whether the required assets are ready, and call [downloadAssets()](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest/downloadassets()) to initiate the download when they are not.

## Topics

### Getting the asset status

### Downloading assets

`func downloadAssets() async throws`
Downloads the assets required to perform the request.

[downloadAssets(progress:)](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest/downloadassets(progress:))
`func downloadAssets(progress: consuming Subprogress) async throws`
Downloads the assets required to perform the request, reporting progress through the provided subprogress.

## See Also

A type for image-analysis requests that focus on a specific part of an image.

The protocol for a type that builds evidence of a condition over time.

A type for analyzing two images together.

[VisionObservation](ref:vision/visionobservation)
`protocol VisionObservation`
A type for objects produced by image-analysis requests.

[VisionRequest](ref:vision/visionrequest)

A type for image-analysis requests.

[DownloadableAssetsRequestStatus](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequeststatus)

The status of the assets required by a [DownloadableAssetsRequest](ref:vision/downloadableassetsrequest).
</content>

<document id="vision/documentobservation/container/barcodes">
<title>barcodes (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 26.0+, iPadOS 26.0+, Mac Catalyst 26.0+, macOS 26.0+, tvOS 26.0+, visionOS 26.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var barcodes: [BarcodeObservation] { get }</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DocumentObservation.Container</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The machine-readable codes found within the container.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Vision recognizes 20 different barcode types; to see the specific codes you can use [supportedBarcodeSymbologies](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/supportedbarcodesymbologies). To see this value, set [enabled](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/barcodedetectionoptions-swift.struct/enabled) within [RecognizeDocumentsRequest.BarcodeDetectionOptions](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/barcodedetectionoptions-swift.struct) to `true`.

## See Also

The lists found within the container.

## Discussion

The framework normalizes this value to `[0, 1]`, where `1` represents the most confident. When results come from a [CoreMLRequest](ref:vision/coremlrequest), the relevant [Core ML](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml) models forward the confidence values.

<document id="vision/visionobservation/confidence">
<title>confidence (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var confidence: Float { get }</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>VisionObservation</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The level of confidence in the observation’s accuracy.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The Vision framework normalizes this value to `[0.0, 1.0]` under most circumstances. A value of `0.0` indicates no confidence. A value of `1.0` indicates highest confidence, or the observation doesn’t support or assign meaning to confidence.

<document id="vision/detectcontoursrequest/contrastadjustment">
<title>contrastAdjustment (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var contrastAdjustment: Float</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectContoursRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The amount by which to adjust the image contrast.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Contour detection works best with high-contrast images. The default value of this property is `2.0`, which doubles the image contrast to achieve the most accurate results.

This property supports a value range from `0.0` to `3.0`.

## See Also

### Configuring a request

[contrastPivot](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/contrastpivot)
`var contrastPivot: Float?`
The pixel value to use as a pivot for the contrast.

[detectsDarkOnLight](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/detectsdarkonlight)
`var detectsDarkOnLight: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether the request detects a dark object on a light background to aid in detection.

[maximumImageDimension](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/maximumimagedimension)
`var maximumImageDimension: Int`
The maximum image dimension to use for contour detection.
</content>
</document>
<document id="vision/detectcontoursrequest/contrastpivot">
<title>contrastPivot (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var contrastPivot: Float?</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectContoursRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The pixel value to use as a pivot for the contrast.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Numeric values range from `0.0` to `1.0`. You can also specify `nil` to have the framework automatically detect the value according to image intensity.

The default value is `0.5`, which indicates the pixel center.

## See Also

### Configuring a request

The amount by which to adjust the image contrast.

A Boolean value that indicates whether the request detects a dark object on a light background to aid in detection.

[maximumImageDimension](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/maximumimagedimension)
`var maximumImageDimension: Int`
The maximum image dimension to use for contour detection.
</content>
</document>

<related>
  <parent>CoreMLRequest</parent>

<purpose>An optional setting that tells the Vision algorithm how to scale an input image.</purpose>

<document id="vision/visionrequest/description">
<title>description (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var description: String { get }</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>VisionRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>A textual representation of this instance.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Calling this property directly is discouraged. Instead, convert an instance of any type to a string by using the `String(describing:)` initializer. This initializer works with any type, and uses the custom `description` property for types that conform to `CustomStringConvertible`:

```swift
struct Point: CustomStringConvertible {
    let x: Int, y: Int

    var description: String {
        return "(\(x), \(y))"
    }
}

let p = Point(x: 21, y: 30)
let s = String(describing: p)
print(s)
// Prints "(21, 30)"
```

The conversion of `p` to a string in the assignment to `s` uses the `Point` type’s `description` property.
</content>
</document>

<related>
  <parent>StatefulRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The reciprocal of the maximum rate to process buffers.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The request won’t process buffers that fall within the [frameAnalysisSpacing](ref:vision/statefulrequest/frameanalysisspacing) since the previously performed analysis. The analysis isn’t done by wall time but by analysis of the time stamps of the sample buffers the request processes.

The heat map is a pixel buffer in a one-component floating-point pixel format.

<related>
  <parent>ClassificationObservation</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The classification label that identifies the type of observation.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

An example classification could be a string like ‘cat’ or ‘hotdog’. The model used for the classification defines the domain of strings that may result. Usually, these strings aren’t localized technical labels not meant for direct presentation to the user.

<document id="vision/detectrectanglesrequest/maximumaspectratio">
<title>maximumAspectRatio (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var maximumAspectRatio: Float</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectRectanglesRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The largest aspect ratio the rectangle request detects.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The property’s value defaults to `1.0`, but you can set it to any value in the range `[0.0, 1.0]`. You can use this value to choose specific rectangles in the detection like filtering out narrow rectangles by excluding small aspect ratios, or setting a range of `0.95` to `1.0` to select mostly squares.

<document id="vision/detecthumanhandposerequest/maximumhandcount">
<title>maximumHandCount (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+</availability>

<related>
  <parent>DetectHumanHandPoseRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The maximum number of hands to detect in an image.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The request orders detected hands by relative size, with only the largest ones having key points determined.

The default value is `2`.

<document id="vision/detectcontoursrequest/maximumimagedimension">
<title>maximumImageDimension (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var maximumImageDimension: Int</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectContoursRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The maximum image dimension to use for contour detection.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Contour detection is computationally intensive. To improve performance, the framework scales the input image down, while maintaining its aspect ratio, such that its maximum dimension is the value of this property. The framework never scales the image up, so specifying the maximum value ensures that the image processes in its original size and not as a downscaled version.

This minimum value supported is `64`. The default value is `512`.

## See Also

### Configuring a request

[contrastAdjustment](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/contrastadjustment)
`var contrastAdjustment: Float`
The amount by which to adjust the image contrast.

[contrastPivot](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/contrastpivot)
`var contrastPivot: Float?`
The pixel value to use as a pivot for the contrast.

[detectsDarkOnLight](ref:vision/detectcontoursrequest/detectsdarkonlight)
`var detectsDarkOnLight: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether the request detects a dark object on a light background to aid in detection.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/detectrectanglesrequest/minimumconfidence">
<title>minimumConfidence (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var minimumConfidence: Float</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectRectanglesRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The minimum acceptable confidence level for detected rectangles.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Vision won’t return rectangles with a confidence score lower than the specified minimum. The property’s default value is `0.0`, but you can set it to any value in the range `[0.0, 1.0]`. A value of `0.0` represents no confidence, while `1.0` represents full confidence.

<document id="vision/statefulrequest/minimumlatencyframecount">
<title>minimumLatencyFrameCount (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>

<related>
  <parent>StatefulRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The minimum number of frames that the request has to process before reporting any observations.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The request provides this information after it’s initialized with its required parameters.

Video-based requests often need a minimum number of frames before they can report any observations. For example, for movement detection that requires at least `5` frames, the [minimumLatencyFrameCount](ref:vision/statefulrequest/minimumlatencyframecount) for the request reports `5`, and after the request processes `5` frames, an observation returns the results.

## See Also

### Inspecting the request

[frameAnalysisSpacing](ref:vision/statefulrequest/frameanalysisspacing)
`var frameAnalysisSpacing: CMTime`
The reciprocal of the maximum rate to process buffers.
</content>
</document>
<document id="vision/detectrectanglesrequest/minimumsize">
<title>minimumSize (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var minimumSize: Float</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectRectanglesRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The minimum size of the rectangle detected as a proportion of the smallest dimension.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The property’s value defaults to `0.2`, but you can set it to any value in the range `[0.0, 1.0]`. Any smaller rectangles that Vision may detect aren’t returned.

## See Also

### Configuring a request

The smallest aspect ratio the rectangle request detects.

[minimumConfidence](ref:vision/detectrectanglesrequest/minimumconfidence)
`var minimumConfidence: Float`
The minimum acceptable confidence level for detected rectangles.

[quadratureToleranceDegrees](ref:vision/detectrectanglesrequest/quadraturetolerancedegrees)
`var quadratureToleranceDegrees: Float`
The maximum number of degrees a rectangle corner angle deviates from 90°.
</content>
</document>
<document id="vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/minimumtextheightfraction">
<title>minimumTextHeightFraction (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 26.0+, iPadOS 26.0+, Mac Catalyst 26.0+, macOS 26.0+, tvOS 26.0+, visionOS 26.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var minimumTextHeightFraction: Float</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>RecognizeDocumentsRequest.TextRecognitionOptions</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The minimum height, relative to the image height, of the text to recognize.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Specify a floating-point number relative to the image height. For example, to limit recognition to text that’s half of the image height, use `0.5`. Increasing the size reduces memory consumption and expedites recognition with the tradeoff of ignoring text smaller than the minimum height. The default value is `1/32`, or `0.03125`.

## See Also

### Inspecting the recognized text

`var customWords: [String]`
An array of strings to supplement the recognized languages at the word-recognition stage.

[maximumCandidateCount](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/maximumcandidatecount)
`var maximumCandidateCount: Int`
The maximum number of text candidates to return.

[recognitionLanguages](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/recognitionlanguages)
`var recognitionLanguages: [Locale.Language]`
An array of languages to detect, in priority order.

[useLanguageCorrection](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/uselanguagecorrection)
`var useLanguageCorrection: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether the request applies language correction during the recognition process.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/trajectoryobservation/projectedpoints">
<title>projectedPoints (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">let projectedPoints: [NormalizedPoint]</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>TrajectoryObservation</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The centroids of the calculated trajectory from the detected points.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The projected points define the ideal trajectory described by the parabolic equation. The equation’s coefficients and the projected points of the detected trajectory get refined over time. The system limits the maximum number of cached points to the maximum points needed to describe the trajectory together with the parabolic equation.

## See Also

### Inspecting an observation

[detectedPoints](ref:vision/trajectoryobservation/detectedpoints)
`let detectedPoints: [NormalizedPoint]`

[equationCoefficients](ref:vision/trajectoryobservation/equationcoefficients)
`let equationCoefficients: simd_float3`
The coefficients of the parabolic equation.

[movingAverageRadius](ref:vision/trajectoryobservation/movingaverageradius)
`let movingAverageRadius: CGFloat`
The moving average radius of the object the request is tracking.
</content>
</document>

<related>

## Discussion

The property’s value defaults to `30`, but you can set it to any value in the range `[0, 45]`.

<document id="vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/recognitionlanguages">
<title>recognitionLanguages (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 26.0+, iPadOS 26.0+, Mac Catalyst 26.0+, macOS 26.0+, tvOS 26.0+, visionOS 26.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var recognitionLanguages: [Locale.Language]</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>RecognizeDocumentsRequest.TextRecognitionOptions</parent>
</related>
<purpose>An array of languages to detect, in priority order.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The order of the languages in the array defines the order in which the system uses languages during language processing and text recognition.

Specify the languages as two-letter ISO language codes.

## See Also

### Inspecting the recognized text

[automaticallyDetectLanguage](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/automaticallydetectlanguage)
`var automaticallyDetectLanguage: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether to attempt detecting the language to use the appropriate model for recognition and language correction.

[customWords](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/customwords)
`var customWords: [String]`
An array of strings to supplement the recognized languages at the word-recognition stage.

[maximumCandidateCount](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/maximumcandidatecount)
`var maximumCandidateCount: Int`
The maximum number of text candidates to return.

[minimumTextHeightFraction](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/minimumtextheightfraction)
`var minimumTextHeightFraction: Float`
The minimum height, relative to the image height, of the text to recognize.

[useLanguageCorrection](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/uselanguagecorrection)
`var useLanguageCorrection: Bool`
A Boolean value that indicates whether the request applies language correction during the recognition process.
</content>
</document>

## Discussion

The order of the languages in the array defines the order in which the system uses languages during language processing and text recognition.

<document id="vision/recognizetextrequest/recognitionlevel-swift.property">
<title>recognitionLevel (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var recognitionLevel: RecognizeTextRequest.RecognitionLevel</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>RecognizeTextRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>A value that determines whether the request prioritizes accuracy or speed in text recognition.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The recognition level determines which techniques the request uses during the text recognition. Set this value to `fast` to prioritize speed over accuracy, and to `accurate` for longer, more computationally intensive recognition.

<document id="vision/imageprocessingrequest/regionofinterest">
<title>regionOfInterest (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var regionOfInterest: NormalizedRect { get set }</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>ImageProcessingRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The region of the image where the framework performs the request.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The system normalizes the rectangle to the dimensions of the processed image. Its origin is the image’s lower-left corner.

The default value is `{ { 0, 0 }, { 1, 1 } }`.
</content>
</document>
<document id="vision/detecttextrectanglesrequest/reportcharacterboxes">
<title>reportCharacterBoxes (Vision)</title>

<related>
  <parent>DetectTextRectanglesRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>A Boolean value that indicates whether the request detects character-bounding boxes.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Set the value to `true` to have the detector return character-bounding boxes as an array of [VNRectangleObservation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/vnrectangleobservation) objects.
</content>
</document>

<related>

</related>
<purpose>A collection of objects describing the distinct areas of the saliency heat map.</purpose>

<document id="vision/faceobservation/capturequality-swift.struct/score">
<title>score (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">let score: Float</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>FaceObservation.CaptureQuality</parent>
</related>
<purpose>A value that indicates the quality of the face capture.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

The score allows you to compare the quality of the face in terms of its capture attributes: lighting, blur, and prime positioning. Use this value to compare the capture quality of a face against other captures of the same face in a specified set. The value of this property value ranges from `0.0` to `1.0`. Faces with quality closer to `1.0` are better lit, sharper, and more centrally positioned than faces with quality closer to `0.0`.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/barcodeobservation/supplementalcompositetype">
<title>supplementalCompositeType (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">let supplementalCompositeType: BarcodeObservation.CompositeType?</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>BarcodeObservation</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The supplemental composite type.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Currently, this can only refer to the composite flag of the 2D symbology as part of a GS1 composite symbology.

This attribute only exists when the primary descriptor is the 1D symbology of a GS1 composite symbology, and of which a valid 2D counterpart has been coalesced into.

## See Also

### Getting the composite type

Composite types for barcode requests.
</content>

<document id="vision/detecttrajectoriesrequest/targetframetime">
<title>targetFrameTime (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">final var targetFrameTime: CMTime { get set }</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectTrajectoriesRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>The requested target frame time for processing trajectory detection.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Use this property value for real-time processing of frames, which requires execution within a specific amount of time. The request evaluates from frame to frame. If processing takes longer than the targeted time for the current frame, it attempts to decrease the overall time by reducing the accuracy (down to a set minimum) for the next frame. If a frame takes less time than the targeted time, the request increases the accuracy (up to a set maximum) of the next frame.

The default value is indefinite, which indicates that accuracy stays at the predefined maximum.

## See Also

### Configuring a request

[objectMaximumNormalizedRadius](ref:vision/detecttrajectoriesrequest/objectmaximumnormalizedradius)
`var objectMaximumNormalizedRadius: Float`
The maximum radius of the bounding circle of the object to track.

[objectMinimumNormalizedRadius](ref:vision/detecttrajectoriesrequest/objectminimumnormalizedradius)
`var objectMinimumNormalizedRadius: Float`
The minimum radius of the bounding circle of the object to track.

[trajectoryLength](ref:vision/detecttrajectoriesrequest/trajectorylength)
`let trajectoryLength: Int`
The number of points to detect before calculating a trajectory.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/uselanguagecorrection">
<title>useLanguageCorrection (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Property</kind>
<availability>iOS 26.0+, iPadOS 26.0+, Mac Catalyst 26.0+, macOS 26.0+, tvOS 26.0+, visionOS 26.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">var useLanguageCorrection: Bool</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>RecognizeDocumentsRequest.TextRecognitionOptions</parent>
</related>
<purpose>A Boolean value that indicates whether the request applies language correction during the recognition process.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

When this value is `true`, Vision applies language correction during the recognition process. When set to `false`, this property returns the raw recognition results, which provides performance benefits but less accurate results.

## See Also

### Inspecting the recognized text

An array of strings to supplement the recognized languages at the word-recognition stage.

[maximumCandidateCount](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/maximumcandidatecount)
`var maximumCandidateCount: Int`
The maximum number of text candidates to return.

[minimumTextHeightFraction](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/minimumtextheightfraction)
`var minimumTextHeightFraction: Float`
The minimum height, relative to the image height, of the text to recognize.

[recognitionLanguages](ref:vision/recognizedocumentsrequest/textrecognitionoptions-swift.struct/recognitionlanguages)
`var recognitionLanguages: [Locale.Language]`
An array of languages to detect, in priority order.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/recognizedtext/boundingbox(for:)">
<title>boundingBox(for:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Method</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">func boundingBox(for range: Range<String.Index>) -> RectangleObservation?</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>RecognizedText</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Calculates the bounding box around the characters in the range of a string.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`range`**: The range of the characters in the text string to draw a bounding box around.

## Return Value

The bounding box surrounding the characters recognized in the image.

## Discussion

Bounding boxes aren’t always an exact fit around the characters. Use them to display in user interfaces to provide general guidance, but avoid using their contents for image processing.

The coordinates of the bounding box are normalized to the dimensions of the processed image, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the image.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/statefulrequest/hash(into:)">
<title>hash(into:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Method</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">func hash(into hasher: inout Hasher)</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>StatefulRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Hashes the essential components of this value by feeding them into the given hasher.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`hasher`**: The hasher to use when combining the components of this instance.

## Discussion

Implement this method to conform to the `Hashable` protocol. The components used for hashing must be the same as the components compared in your type’s `==` operator implementation. Call `hasher.combine(_:)` with each of these components.

> **Important:** In your implementation of `hash(into:)`, don’t call `finalize()` on the `hasher` instance provided, or replace it with a different instance. Doing so may become a compile-time error in the future.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/classificationobservation/hasminimumprecision(_:forrecall:)">
<title>hasMinimumPrecision(_:forRecall:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Method</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">func hasMinimumPrecision(_ minimumPrecision: Float, forRecall recall: Float) -> Bool</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>ClassificationObservation</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Determines whether the observation has a minimum precision value for a specific recall.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`minimumPrecision`**: The minimum desired percentage of correct positive classifications.
- **`recall`**: The percentage of all positive classifications that the algorithm correctly classified.

## Return Value

A Boolean value that indicates whether the classification observation provides a minimum percentage of correct results that meet the desired recall.

## Discussion

The following example uses the `hasMinimumPrecision(_:forRecall)` method to perform a high-recall filter on the results of a `ClassifyImageRequest`:

```swift
let results = try await request.perform(on: image)
    .filter { $0.hasMinimumPrecision(0.1, forRecall: 0.8) }
```

A high-recall filter retains a much broader range of observations, but can result in more false positive results. Testing can help determine the balance point between the `minimumPrecision` and `recall` values to return the best results for a specific use case.

## See Also

### Determining precision and recall

[hasMinimumRecall(_:forPrecision:)](ref:vision/classificationobservation/hasminimumrecall(_:forprecision:))
`func hasMinimumRecall(Float, forPrecision: Float) -> Bool`
Determines whether the observation has a minimum recall value for a specific precision.
</content>
</document>
<document id="vision/classificationobservation/hasminimumrecall(_:forprecision:)">
<title>hasMinimumRecall(_:forPrecision:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Method</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">func hasMinimumRecall(_ minimumRecall: Float, forPrecision precision: Float) -> Bool</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>ClassificationObservation</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Determines whether the observation has a minimum recall value for a specific precision.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`minimumRecall`**: The minimum desired percentage of all positive classifications that the algorithm correctly classifies.
- **`precision`**: The percentage of correct positive classifications.

## Return Value

A Boolean value that indicates whether the classification observation achieves a minimum recall value for a specific precision.

## Discussion

The following example uses the `hasMinimumRecall(_:forPrecision)` method to perform a high-precision filter on the results of a `ClassifyImageRequest`.

```swift
let results = try await request.perform(on: image)
    .filter { $0.hasMinimumRecall(0.01, forPrecision: 0.9) }
```

A high-precision filter retains a smaller number of observations, with less chance to contain false positives. Testing can help determine the balance point between the `minimumRecall` and `precision` values to return the best results for a specific use case.

## See Also

### Determining precision and recall

[hasMinimumPrecision(_:forRecall:)](ref:vision/classificationobservation/hasminimumprecision(_:forrecall:))
`func hasMinimumPrecision(Float, forRecall: Float) -> Bool`
Determines whether the observation has a minimum precision value for a specific recall.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/visionrequest/setcomputedevice(_:for:)">
<title>setComputeDevice(_:for:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Instance Method</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">mutating func setComputeDevice(_ computeDevice: MLComputeDevice?, for computeStage: ComputeStage)</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>VisionRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Assigns a compute device for a compute stage.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`computeDevice`**: The compute device to assign to the compute stage.
- **`computeStage`**: The compute stage.

## Discussion

If the parameter `computeDevice` is `nil`, the framework removes any explicit compute device assignment and allows the framework to select the device.

Configure any compute device for a given compute stage. When performing a request, the system makes a validity check. Use [supportedComputeStageDevices](ref:vision/visionrequest/supportedcomputestagedevices) to get valid compute devices for a request’s compute stages.
</content>
</document>

No result will be produced if the box is outside the `regionOfInterest`. By default, the `regionOfInterest` is the whole image.

<document id="vision/detecttrajectoriesrequest/init(trajectorylength:_:frameanalysisspacing:)">
<title>init(trajectoryLength:_:frameAnalysisSpacing:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Initializer</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">init(trajectoryLength: Int, _ revision: DetectTrajectoriesRequest.Revision? = nil, frameAnalysisSpacing: CMTime? = nil)</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectTrajectoriesRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Creates a trajectory-detection request.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`trajectoryLength`**: The number of points required to analyze to determine that a shape follows a parabolic path. This argument value must be at least 5.
- **`revision`**: The specific algorithm or implementation revision that the system uses to perform the request.
- **`frameAnalysisSpacing`**: The duration between analysis operations. Increase this value to reduce the number of frames analyzed on slower devices. By default, Vision analyzes all frames.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/statefulrequest/==(_:_:)">
<title>==(_:_:) (Vision)</title>
<kind>Operator</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">static func == (lhs: Self, rhs: Self) -> Bool</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>StatefulRequest</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Returns a Boolean value indicating whether two values are equal.</purpose>
<content>
## Parameters

- **`lhs`**: A value to compare.
- **`rhs`**: Another value to compare.

## Discussion

Equality is the inverse of inequality. For any values `a` and `b`, `a == b` implies that `a != b` is `false`.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/detectfacelandmarksrequest/revision-swift.enum/revision4">

<kind>Case</kind>
<availability>iOS 27.0+, iPadOS 27.0+, Mac Catalyst 27.0+, macOS 27.0+, tvOS 27.0+, visionOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">case revision4</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>DetectFaceLandmarksRequest.Revision</parent>
</related>
<purpose>This revision uses [DetectFaceRectanglesRequest.Revision.revision4](ref:vision/detectfacerectanglesrequest/revision-swift.enum/revision4) for detecting faces and then detects 98 face landmark points, providing more detailed results than the previous revision. This is the default revision on platforms that support it. Specify `.revision3` at instantiation to preserve the previous behavior. Use [supportedRevisions](ref:vision/detectfacelandmarksrequest/supportedrevisions) to check if this revision is supported on the platform.</purpose>

<related>
  <parent>DetectFaceRectanglesRequest.Revision</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Compared to `.revision3`, this revision generally provides better precision and recall, and bounding boxes tend to be tighter. This is the default revision on platforms that support it. <document id="vision/imagecropandscaleaction/scaletofillplus90ccwrotation">
<title>ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFillPlus90CCWRotation (Vision)</title>
<kind>Case</kind>
<availability>iOS 18.0+, iPadOS 18.0+, Mac Catalyst 18.0+, macOS 15.0+, tvOS 18.0+, visionOS 2.0+, watchOS 27.0+</availability>
<declaration language="swift">case scaleToFillPlus90CCWRotation</declaration>
<related>
  <parent>ImageCropAndScaleAction</parent>
</related>
<purpose>An action that scales the image and rotates it by 90 degrees counter clockwise.</purpose>
<content>
## Discussion

Rotation helps to optimize portrait images fit into landscape buffers for algorithms that are rotation agnostic.

## See Also

### Getting the actions

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.centerCrop](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)
`case centerCrop`
An action that scales the image and maintains the aspect ratio to fit on the short side and crop centered on the long side.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFit](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)
`case scaleToFit`
An action that scales to the size the algorithm requires while maintaining the original aspect ratio.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFill](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction)
`case scaleToFill`
An action that scales the image to fill the input dimensions and resizing it, if necessary.

[ImageCropAndScaleAction.scaleToFitPlus90CCWRotation](ref:vision/imagecropandscaleaction/scaletofitplus90ccwrotation)
`case scaleToFitPlus90CCWRotation`
An action that scales the image and maintains the aspect ratio to fit on the long side, and rotates the image by 90 degrees counter clockwise.
</content>
</document>

<document id="vision/supporting-pose-types">
<title>Supporting Pose Types (Vision)</title>
<kind>API Collection</kind>
<related>
  <parent>Vision</parent>
</related>
<purpose>Types you use when working with pose analysis.</purpose>
<content>
## Overview

Use these types when working with pose detection results to access joint information and properties.

## Topics

### Joints

[Joint](ref:vision/joint)
`struct Joint`
A pose joint represented as a normalized point in an image, along with a label and a confidence value.

[Joint3D](ref:vision/joint3d)
`struct Joint3D`
An object that represents a body pose joint in 3D space.

### Handedness

[Chirality](ref:vision/chirality)
`enum Chirality`
The hand sidedness of a pose.

## See Also

### Pose analysis

[DetectAnimalBodyPoseRequest](ref:vision/detectanimalbodyposerequest)
`struct DetectAnimalBodyPoseRequest`
A request that detects an animal body pose.

[DetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest](ref:vision/detecthumanbodypose3drequest)
`class DetectHumanBodyPose3DRequest`
A request that detects points on human bodies in 3D space, relative to the camera.

[DetectHumanBodyPoseRequest](ref:vision/detecthumanbodyposerequest)
`struct DetectHumanBodyPoseRequest`
A request that detects a human body pose.

[DetectHumanHandPoseRequest](ref:vision/detecthumanhandposerequest)
`struct DetectHumanHandPoseRequest`
A request that detects a human hand pose.
</content>
</document>
